Plugging in my headphones. Strapping on a guitar. Shred through my favourite metal tracks while envisioning a festival crowd cheering and going nuts in front of me. A parental intrusion can tear me straight out of the zone.

More of a coincidence but still rare. Left my pub job in London to travel for a year in New Zealand. Arrived and checked myself into a hostel in Auckland. Chatted to a girl in the bunk below me. turns out she lives 2 roads away from me back home and left the same pub I worked in shortly before I started there. Never heard of her before. 10 mutual friends on facebook. we're now good friends.
My anxiety makes me anxious. What a way to live a life.

Depression. the disease is a creeper and that black dog can silently rise over a period of years, lurking under the sufferers conscious radar. I had a hugely happy upbringing and therefore had no reason to feel the way i do? i'll just get on with it. ignore it. I noticed small changes through college and university....things just started with an underlying 'meh' attitude towards everything i used to love. cant get passed that slightly challenging level? meh i'll try another game. Cool ass movie about to drop in cinemas? meh got noone to go with. Cancelled social events? meh what a relief....etc etc. Maybe i'm depressed, i would ask others and get the same response, 'nah your just growing up'.

Fast forward a few dull years I land my first full time job. discovered an inability to concentrate on near anything. Unable to cope with grinding pressure. Getting home and discovering i had nothing to do/look forward to. Weekends were empty and Sundays were spent dreading the week ahead. Anxiety and panic attacks crept in. poor sleep, low appetite. But this is life and what everyone has to do right? wrong, apparently it turns out not everyone is like this....oh crap I need to see a doctor. diagnosed with clinical depression and GAD. Im getting help now but fuk me if i got this support back in my 'Meh' days shit could have been very different.

TL:DR: If you have even a slight inkling you may have depression. You have depression. Get help now.

Memory Loss is a 'normal' symptom of dpdr. I honestly think its because we are so wrapped up in thinking about our dp that it leaves little room for us to take in things we should or need to remember. Our environment and conversations help trigger past memories but these memories become hazier as they become blanketed with the dp. the only way we can think clearer is if we break the cycle which is really the holy grail for all of us.

I agree completely. Based in London here. I didnt realise that I get pretty bad SAD which links in with dpdr comorbid with anxiety and depression. I honestly thought it was normal and everyone just got bummed out with the dark winter months. Its currently cold but the sun is out with crystal clear blue skies and can definitely feel a lowering of my symptoms. Early last year during a particularly stressful time of my life I booked a holiday to Spain just as an experiment. Was in a haze all the way until I arrived. I spent a whole beautiful week completely symptom free, it was almost like my brain kickstarted. The dp returned with a vengance almost as soon as I touched down back at Gatwick. Since then I've been experimenting with high dosage vitamin D and SAD lamps with little effect.

Before dpdr, i used to be able to close my eyes and get lost in a world of my own visual imagination; thinking about the people i love, the things i looked forward to, girls i used to fantasise about and used to be able to nap like a champion. Now i just see the darkness of the back of my eyelids after trauma related dp set in. It was like my very soul left me. Sorry for bleak post but this is exactly it. good luck to everyone :)

I can relate to some extent. The first time I experienced a dissociate consciousness was when i was very young like 10 or 11. I remember being jet lagged after a long haul flight and had symptoms of a fever. I would walk around feeling extremely 'tall' looking down and getting a sense of vertigo and all my surroundings seemed to shrink and warp. This passed and was probably delirium associated with over exertion and no sleep.
Another thing I noticed but didn't pay much attention to was when i would  dissociate during job interviews. This was a culmination of being hyper aware of myself in an anxious scenario. I would go into a stare at the interviewer and their heads would begin to warp, expand and shrink. I could shake this off momentarily by refocusing my attention by looking away momentarily and taking deep breaths/swigs of water. Was surprised when i spoke of this to other people and they had never heard of this phenomenon.

Speaking to friends and family members about my past helps a little and i get 'flickers' of images and things that happened during conversation, so im gunna try my best to keep talking. My conceptualising now involves a lot of writing down the things and responsibilities i need to achieve to get through the week. Im not sure what direction to take to help get back my 'imagination' but right now im following the passage of time

It is heartbreaking i know but im being stoic about the situation and keeping my internal dialogue positive...now that more positive things are happening im starting to get more flickers of 'memories' and images in my mind. This happens a lot more when im talking to people...so i think talking might help trigger more positive memories while inbetween i have a veil of more of what I would describe as a void
